# Verification log

Recorded results of checks. Each entry states the date, environment, command, and outcome. Never record a result that was not observed. Package, element, file, and token names in every entry use the current naming contract ([ADR 0037](./architecture/decisions/0037-naming-contract.md)).

**Evidence vocabulary.** Plan and architecture status uses: *implemented and verified* (entry below), *implemented with remaining verification*, *planned*, *experimental*, and *explicitly deferred*. Selected verification results use `selected`, `passed`, `failed`, `reused` (with the reused baseline's conditions), `not-executed`, and `unresolved` ([change-impact-and-verification.md](./architecture/change-impact-and-verification.md) §2.4). Results name the implementation, configuration, browser and version, and suite version they apply to; automated results never stand in for manual accessibility evidence, and a navigation test that only calls "go back" is not back/forward cache evidence.

**Environment:** Windows, Node 24.19.0, npm 11.17.0, TypeScript 7.0.2, Vitest 5.0.5, Playwright 1.64.1 (Chrome for Testing 156.0.8078.4, Firefox 157.0, WebKit 27.2), Prettier 3.9.10, es-module-lexer 3.0.4, Ajv 8 + ajv-formats 3.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build | `npm run build` | Pass — 5 packages + `apps/docs` built with `tsc -b` (ESM + declarations + maps) |
| Boundaries | `npm run lint:boundaries` | Pass — 6 packages, 6 source files, 10 imports; manifests, sources, built artifacts, and the DOM-free `@oddkin/tokens` entry checked |
| Deliberate violation | Added `import '@oddkin/state'` to `packages/components/src/index.ts`, ran the checker, reverted | Fails as intended: `✖ [boundary.import.forbidden] @oddkin/components may not import @oddkin/state.` with file and fix |
| Formatting | `npm run format:check` | Pass |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck` | Pass — packages, tests, e2e, and configs |
| Unit tests | `npm test` | Pass — 29 tests: 5 package skeleton tests, 11 boundary-checker tests (temporary fixture workspaces), 13 schema tests |
| Full pipeline | `npm run verify` | Pass — lint, typecheck, unit tests, browser tests, packed consumers in one run |
| Browser tests | `npm run test:e2e` | Pass — plain-HTML consumer loads every package through an import map in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with no page errors |
| Packed consumers | `npm run verify:packs` | Pass — 5 tarballs installed into a temporary project outside the workspace; runtime imports and declarations resolve; no third-party runtime dependencies installed |

**Finding during M1:** the first boundary run reported "OK" while scanning zero imports, because es-module-lexer 3 renamed the import field (`n` → `specifier`). Fixed; the checker now reports scan counts and fails if source files yield no imports, and a test asserts side-effect and type-only imports are counted.

**Not yet verified:** the CI workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) has not run (no remote configured). Minimum browser versions from ADR 0009 are not yet tested; only current Playwright builds were used.
## 2026-10-17 — M3 core reactivity and `Scope`

**Environment:** as M1.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reactive graph | `npx vitest run packages/core` | Pass — 37 tests: signal equality/no-op writes, lazy memoized computed, diamond glitch-freedom, dynamic dependencies, unchanged-derivation suppression, cached errors, cycles (`reactive.cycle`), writes in computed, nested batches, reentrant subscribers, runaway detection, effect phases, cleanup ordering, self-writing effects, self-disposal, error isolation, `untracked`, `settled` |
| `Scope` | `npx vitest run packages/core` | Pass — 16 tests: reverse-order cleanup, early release, error isolation (`scope.cleanup.error` with origin), disposed-scope no-ops, abort reason, listener removal and options, timeouts/intervals (fake timers, `scope.timer.error`), child disposal and detachment, per-run effect scopes, controllers |
| Leak baseline | `scope.test.ts` "returns to baseline after 1,000 mount/dispose cycles" | Pass — internal scope/listener/timer/effect counts return to the starting values |
| DOM-free entries | `npm run lint:boundaries` | Pass — `@oddkin/core/reactive` and `@oddkin/core/scope` import in Node without DOM globals; 6 packages, 11 source files, 21 imports |
| Full pipeline | `npm run verify` | Pass — 81 unit tests, 3 browser tests (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit), packed consumers |

**Findings:** (1) registering an observer on a computed marked it stale and suppressed later pushes; fixed by forcing a global-version recheck instead. (2) An effect that writes a source it read must re-run; effects now compare source versions after each run and reschedule, with runaway detection. (3) `tsc` rejected test mocks returning values from effects — the `EffectFn` return type (void or cleanup) is enforced as intended.

**Not yet measured:** collection update cost, size, startup, and memory (M3 measurements).
## 2026-10-17 — M3 templates, styles, elements, and the property API

**Environment:** as M1, plus `@vitest/browser-playwright` 5.0.5 (dev-only) running Vitest browser tests in the same Playwright builds.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Template lexer | `npx vitest run --project node packages/core` | Pass — case-preserved attribute names, multi-value attributes, comments/raw text ignored; stable codes for tag-name, attribute-name, comment, raw-text, mixed, `on*`, `innerHTML`/`srcdoc`, and unclosed positions |
| Templates (browser) | `npx vitest run --project browser` | Pass in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit — text never parsed as markup; in-place text and nested-instance reuse; nodes, arrays; functions not called; direct readable bindings without re-render; attribute/boolean/property parts; one DOM mutation per change (MutationObserver); subscription release; stable event listener with host `this`; `when`/`match`; keyed `repeat` reuse, release, duplicate-key diagnostic; focus kept across updates; SVG namespace; `javascript:` URLs blocked |
| Elements (browser) | same | Pass in all three — counter clicks update without `render()`; tracked `.value` reads re-render once per flush; dual-path value written once; handler reads untracked; typed defaults; per-instance object/array defaults; attribute conversion and boolean presence; invalid values reported with fallback; reflection opt-in on commit; pre-upgrade replay; reserved/duplicate names and attributes rejected; shadowing class field reported; `with()` chaining; hook order and one `updated` per batch; disconnect disposes listeners, reconnect resumes retained nodes with latest state; async generation guard; `moveBefore` keeps the connection (where supported); hook/render errors isolated with previous DOM kept; events, custom states, `define()` idempotence/collision/dependencies/name validation |
| Leak baseline (browser) | element test "1,000 connect/disconnect cycles" | Pass — scope/listener/timer/effect counts return to baseline |
| Shared styles | element test "100 instances" | Pass — one constructed sheet per document; iframe adoption swaps to that document's sheet; `<style>` fallback carries the nonce and is replaced on re-adoption |
| Declaration emit | `npm run typecheck` (`tests/examples/core-counter.types.test.ts`) | Pass — consumer types from emitted `.d.ts`: `string`, `boolean`, enum union, `string[]`, event detail, tag-name map |
| Static analyzability | `tests/experiments/analyzability.test.ts` | Pass — TypeScript 7 `unstable/sync` API extracts full property metadata from source in ~0.5 s; fixture module that throws on import is never executed; dynamic spreads, computed keys, and non-literal options yield `analyzer.dynamic.*` |
| Strict CSP + Trusted Types | `npx playwright test e2e/core-counter.spec.ts` | Pass in all three; zero `securitypolicyviolation` events under `default-src 'none'; style-src 'self'; require-trusted-types-for 'script'`; Trusted Types confirmed **enforced** in Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2 |
| DOM-free import | `npm run lint:boundaries` | Pass — every `@oddkin/core` entry (root, `reactive`, `scope`, `template`, `styles`, `element`, `diagnostics`) imports in Node without DOM globals; `@oddkin/state` now depends on `@oddkin/core/reactive` only |
| Full pipeline | `npm run verify` | Pass — 90 Node + 147 browser unit tests, 6 e2e, packed consumers |

**Findings:** (1) TypeScript 7.0.2 has no in-process compiler API; only `typescript/unstable/*` (IPC) — recorded in ADR 0018. (2) A trailing `<` before a binding (`<${tag}>`) was lexed as text; now rejected as a dynamic tag name. (3) Importing the core root in Node threw (`HTMLElement` undefined), which would also break server imports in framework apps; the base class now falls back to a stub and `define()` is a no-op without a registry. (4) Import-map consumers need an entry for every subpath loaded transitively (`@oddkin/core/reactive`).

**Data point, not a measurement:** unminified `@oddkin/core` output with comments is 87.7 KB raw / 21.7 KB gzip in total (template 8.6 KB, element 6.7 KB, reactive 4.2 KB gzip). Minified per-entry sizes, startup, update, and memory measurements remain M3 work.

## 2026-10-17 — M2 conditions, profiles, and unit policy

**Environment:** as the previous entry.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Conditions | `packages/tokens/test/conditions-profiles.test.ts` | Pass — named and unnamed container queries (logical and physical sizes), media ranges and preference features serialize to literal `{ kind, query, atRule }`; `@oddkin/tokens/conditions` imports without a DOM; `var()`, `%`, unitless, logical media sizes, invalid preference values, empty ranges, reserved container names, missing features, and unknown kinds report codes and paths; `px` thresholds warn |
| Profiles | same | Pass — attribute-scoped overrides with alias closure; nested-scope re-application selector emitted; profiles after products and densities; only layout/component roles; unknown roles, invalid values, missing references, and tier violations reported under `/profiles/…`; overlaps warn and name the winner; target minimums checked per profile and per profile × density for affected roles only |
| Unit policy | same | Pass — unitless line heights, font weights 1–1000, lengths with units; `px` warns for type and control sizes, not borders |
| Cascade | `packages/tokens/test/generate.browser.test.ts` | Pass in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit — a profile applies in dark mode and **survives inside a nested compact density**; lengths compared within 0.05px because WebKit snaps margins to 1/64px (`0.8438rem` → 13.5px vs 13.5008px elsewhere) |
| CSS-only page | `npx playwright test e2e/tokens-css-only.spec.ts` | Pass in all three under light and dark preferences — profile padding, and profile + nested compact density, equal `resolveToken()` |
| Full pipeline | `npm run verify` | Pass — 149 Node + 240 browser unit tests, 12 e2e, packed consumers |

**Findings:** (1) A profile changes role expressions, so a nested density/product/mode/theme scope would re-declare base expressions and drop it; each profile rule also targets nested scopes inside its subtree. (2) CSS cannot honour `data-odd-profile` list order; precedence follows configuration order and overlaps are reported. (3) Preset profiles originally referenced `space.2xs`, which custom scales need not define; they now derive smaller values with `calc()` from required steps. (4) Duplicate unit diagnostics and repeated target unit-mismatch warnings were removed.

## 2026-10-17 — M3 measurements, development/production builds, size budgets

Environment: Windows 11 (10.0.26300), Intel i5-1135G7 (8 threads), 16 GiB, Node 24.19, Playwright 1.64.1 headless (Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2), esbuild 0.28.2. Raw samples, medians, and p95 are in `research/benchmarks/results/2026-10-17-win32.json`; the method is recorded in that file and in `research/benchmarks/run.mjs`.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Production build | `npx vitest run --project node packages/core/test/production.test.ts` | Pass — `dist/prod` has the same modules and export names as `dist`; every export maps `types`/`development`/`default`; Node resolves production by default and development with `--conditions=development`; production errors keep `[code]` (for example `reactive.write.inComputed`) with a pointer to the development build; no development message text or `DEV` reference remains |
| Size budgets | `npm run size` (part of `npm run verify`) | Pass — production gzip: minimal counter 9,280 B (budget 9,728), typical component 10,553 B, keyed list 11,064 B, reactive-only 1,892 B; no component bundle includes state, app, or tokens. The 8 KiB counter target was missed and revised in ADR 0031 |
| Keyed `repeat` | `npx vitest run packages/core/test/template.browser.test.ts` | Pass in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit — focused input that itself moves keeps focus and selection; 60 seeded rounds of shuffles, inserts, removals, and reversals keep order and reuse every surviving node |
| Mount/update | `node research/benchmarks/run.mjs` (15 samples, 3 warm-ups) | 1,000 counters, median ms: mount 11–15 (Chromium), 25–51 (Firefox), 11–15 (WebKit, one noisy run had p95 182); increment all and flush 1.4–2.3 / 4–7 / 2–3; one counter of 1,000 updated and flushed in ≈ 3–10 µs |
| Collection vs handwritten `repeat` | same | At 1,000 items, Chromium median ms (collection / handwritten): replace 1.6 / 1.4, single edit 0.8 / 0.7, insert 1.0 / 0.7–0.8, remove 0.8–1.3 / 0.5–0.9, reverse 2.2–3.5 / 2.0–2.8. Firefox 1–2 ms, reverse 5–7. WebKit 1–5 ms, reverse 9–28 across runs. The collection layer costs about 0–30% over a plain array signal. At 10 and 100 items every operation is under 1 ms in all engines |
| Memory (Chromium, CDP) | same | Retained per mounted counter ≈ 2.3 KB. Retained list at 1,000 items: collection ≈ 567 KB, handwritten ≈ 482 KB. Allocation per full replace at 1,000: ≈ 646 KB / ≈ 497 KB. Values at 10 items are within GC noise |
| Ownership and leaks | same | `scopeStats()` returns exactly to baseline (0 scopes, listeners, timers, effects) after 100 cycles of mounting and removing 100 counters in all three engines; Chromium heap after 106 cycles is within 5 KB of the heap after the first cycle |

**Findings:** (1) **WebKit list reorders were quadratic.** Without `moveBefore`, per-item `insertBefore` of `<li>` renumbers following list items on every move. Raw DOM took 239 ms to reverse 1,000 `<li>` in a `<ul>` and 1.6 s in an `<ol>`, versus 3 ms for `<div>`, and our `repeat` took 319 ms. The fallback now detaches moved ranges from the end of the list and inserts each run as one fragment: 9–28 ms across runs. Chromium and Firefox keep state-preserving `moveBefore`. (2) The keyed reconciler was bundled into every template; it now ships only with `repeat()`. (3) Development messages were about 1.7 KB gzip of the counter. (4) Port 4190 is on the Fetch blocked-port list, so the runner uses 4183. (5) Firefox and WebKit clamp `performance.now()` to about 1 ms without cross-origin isolation, so small operations run over independent copies and are averaged. (6) Firefox mounts direct-binding counters more slowly than render-tracked ones (40–51 vs 25–28 ms per 1,000); recorded for the binding walkthrough.

## 2026-10-17 — M3 binding-rule walkthrough and failure paths

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Binding rule (plain JS and TS) | `npx playwright test e2e/binding-rule.spec.ts` | Pass in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit — identical tables for elements authored in plain JavaScript (no build) and TypeScript: direct binding 0 renders / 1 write for three writes; render-tracked 1 / 1; dual path 1 / 1 (coalesced); handler and async snapshots 0 / 0 and read current values; no-op 0 / 0; public property 1 / 1 with `updated(label)`; same value 0 / 0; attribute 1 / 1; DOM unchanged before `updateComplete`, updated after |
| Failure paths | `npx vitest run packages/core/test/failure-paths.browser.test.ts` | Pass in all three (13 tests): invalid attribute falls back and recovers; throwing derivation in `render()` keeps the last DOM, reports `reactive.effect.error` with origin `<tag> render`, and recovers; a throwing direct binding leaves sibling bindings updating without a re-render; failing effect does not stop others in the flush; throwing setter reported and later values written; all cleanups run with one `scope.cleanup.error`; throwing `mounted()` leaves rendering working; shared module signal unsubscribes per removed element; self-removing handler leaves no subscriptions or owned resources; disconnect during a flush cancels the other element's queued effect; six connections get six scopes with no listener accumulation; direct updates make no layout reads (spied getters, `getBoundingClientRect`, `getComputedStyle`) and no re-render; production build in the browser reports the same code and owner with the short message |

**Findings:** (1) A test element named its handler `remove`, shadowing `Element.remove()`; the type check (`noImplicitOverride`) caught it. Worth a note in authoring docs: instance members on an `OddkinElement` share the `HTMLElement` namespace. (2) No core behavior changes were needed: the failure contract held as documented.

**Findings:** (1) `oddkin-metadata.v1` stores `library.prefix` with its trailing hyphen and example references as component ids (`component:<tag>`); the registry accepts both forms. (3) `verify-packs` assumed every package had a root entry; it now checks subpath-only packages. (4) As the suite grew, a process-spawning CLI test exceeded 5 s on a busy machine; it now has the analyzer's 30 s budget.

## 2026-10-17 — M3 startup and update-to-paint

Command: `node research/benchmarks/run.mjs --samples 15` (results regenerated in `research/benchmarks/results/2026-10-17-win32.json`; this run was on a busy shared machine, and timings were 1.2–2× slower than earlier runs: Chromium mount of 1,000 counters 18 ms vs 11–15 ms).

| Measure (median, p95 ms) | Chromium 156 | Firefox 157 | WebKit 27.2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| First render after navigation start, cold context, minimal production counter | 36, 46 | 169, 367 | 46, 60 |
| Bundle response end → first render (parse, execute, define, render) | 7.4 | 18 | 33 |
| Click → next frame, Oddkin counter | 9.2, 11.5 | 3, 9 | 27, 42 |
| Click → next frame, plain-DOM control button | 9.8, 16.4 | 3, 10 | 26, 39 |
| Clicks over 16 ms by Event Timing (both buttons) | 12 of 90 | 0 of 90 | 46 of 90 |

**Findings:** (1) Oddkin's click-to-next-frame time matches the plain-DOM control in every engine, so the update itself adds no measurable frame latency. WebKit's ~27 ms comes from headless WebKit's frame scheduling and affects the control equally. (2) Firefox's first render includes a slower cold context start (median 169 ms after navigation start) while its script-to-render time is 18 ms. (3) Timing on this machine varies between sessions; these are baselines for regression review (plan §8: flag > 15% timing change), not cross-library comparisons.

Reusing the published class for another name reports `analyzer.dynamic.definition`. |
| Publisher without facts | same file | `tests/fixtures/analyzer-legacy` vendors a package with a CEM and definition facts but no per-source facts, plus an undocumented element class. Results: `analyzer.published.sources` (info) and `analyzer.published.missing` (warning); the undocumented class's subclass is left out; the legacy token read is kept rather than guessed away. |
| Existing outputs | `npx vitest run --project node packages/analyzer tests/schemas packages/components/test/metadata.test.ts packages/ai/test/metadata.test.ts packages/workbench` | Pass. The committed `core-counter` fixture gains only the `templates` and `styles` sections. `node scripts/build-metadata.mjs` reports no diagnostics for `@oddkin/components` and `@oddkin/ai`. The AI package now records the shared styles it imports with `package` and the publisher's reads. |
| Mutation probes | temporary edits, reverted | Without published-definition spreads: 3 failures, including the legacy case. Without published style reads in the overlay: 1 failure, the token-read test. |

**Findings:** (1) Published CEM and definition facts were enough for the contract, but not for replacing a skin accurately: the per-component CSS properties and token reads do not say which style source provided them, so per-source facts were added. (2) Template anatomy is published per template for the same reason: a replaced template must drop the slots and parts only the old one rendered.

## 2026-10-19 — Container, wrapper, and region contract (M2)

Environment as the previous entry. Contract: [layout-recipes.md §5](./architecture/layout-recipes.md#5-container-responsive-composition), [css-architecture.md §5.4](./architecture/css-architecture.md#54-selectors-and-customization-surface).

| Evidence level | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser (plain shadow roots) | `npx vitest run --project browser packages/core/test/container-contract.browser.test.ts` | Pass (8 × 3 engines). An element that is its own query container never matches its own query; its descendants do. Inline-size containment gives an inline-block and an absolutely positioned box zero width (shrink-to-fit ignores content). Slotted light-DOM content resolves both an unnamed page query and the shadow tree's `::slotted()` query against a region inside the shadow tree (flat-tree ancestry). An unnamed query uses the nearest container; a named query skips to the named one. `::slotted()` styles top-level slotted elements only; a compound `::slotted(p) span` matches nothing. `::part()` reaches the declared part only: not its descendants, not `::part()[attr]`, and not a nested component's part unless forwarded with `exportparts`. Page selectors never match private shadow markup with the same class names. An inherited role reaches shadow internals, slotted content, and a nested shadow root, and a declaration on a region wins inside it. |
| Finding | same test | Container names are **not** encapsulated in Chromium, Firefox, or WebKit: a page query `@container region (…)` styles slotted content against a container named `region` inside the component's shadow tree. Internal container names are therefore public; the contract now says to name only the host (as Oddkin recipes do) or to namespace internal names. |
| Existing | `packages/core/test/layout.browser.test.ts`, `packages/components/test/styling.browser.test.ts`, `side-nav.browser.test.ts`, `tests/floor/probe.js` | Unchanged: a host container responds per instance, roles reach slotted content, parts and component variables override, page selectors never reach button internals, and container queries work in the floor browsers. |

**Not covered:** floor-browser runs of the new checks (the floor probe covers basic container queries only).

| --- | --- | --- |
| Engine behavior | Temporary probes (not kept): Enter in fields of forms with `odd-input`, native inputs, `odd-button`, and native submit buttons; computed styles of disabled buttons | Same in Chromium, Firefox, WebKit: Enter in an `odd-input` never submits (its inner input has no form owner), even with a native submit button; Enter in a form's only text field submits with no submitter when the only submit button is an `odd-button`, and does nothing with two text fields; a native submit button is the default button. Disabled `odd-button`s kept their appearance's background (finding 2) |
| Button | `npx vitest run --project browser packages/components/test/button.browser.test.ts` | Pass in three engines (16 tests): `formaction`, `formmethod`, `formenctype`, `formtarget`, `formnovalidate` reflect and reach the temporary submitter, which `formnovalidate` lets past an empty required field; without overrides the submitter carries none; reassociation through `form` and a move submits the new owner and nothing outside a form; Enter submits with no submitter or through a native button, never through `odd-button`; `form.requestSubmit(oddButton)` throws `TypeError` |
| Input | `npx vitest run --project browser packages/components/test/input.browser.test.ts` | Pass in three engines (15 tests): Enter in the field does not submit; a native button does |
| Native-button path | `npx vitest run --project browser packages/components/test/styling.browser.test.ts`, `npx vitest run --project node packages/components/test/styles.test.ts` | Pass in three engines: 25 computed properties of `<button class="odd-button">` equal the `odd-button` control's in 36 cases (3 appearances × 3 sizes × enabled/disabled × light/dark), by default, with all six `--odd-button-*` variables, and at full width; same focus ring; hover reaches the same `action.hover`/`surface.hover` colours. `button.css` starts with the canonical layer order, keeps its rules in `odd.components`, and has no `!important` |
| Real submissions | `npx playwright test e2e/forms.spec.ts` (fixture `tests/forms/`) | Pass in three engines (2 tests; 24 of 24 with `--repeat-each=4`). Requests intercepted with `page.route`: GET with `item` and `intent`; the draft button's POST, multipart body, and `drafts` frame, with an empty required field; a blocked submission (`invalid` fired, nothing sent); a text/plain POST to the form's own action and frame. Each `odd-button` request equals the request of a native submit button with the same attributes. The submitter is a `button` disconnected after dispatch. The native `.odd-button` is the submitter and the default button for Enter, has the primary background from the tokens, and an `odd-button` outside the form submits it through `form` |
| CSS | `npm run lint:css`, `npm run compat`, `npm run size` | 58 stylesheets; `components:button` 1,150 B (1,119 B before the disabled fix); new `components:button.css` budget 1,024 B, measured 864 B |
| Full pipeline | `npm run verify` steps one by one (`npm test -- --reporter=verbose`, then `npm run verify:metadata` directly after it) | Lint: boundaries and CSS compatibility pass; formatting failed only on the other agent's uncommitted `references.ts` and `build-metadata.mjs`. Typecheck, size, e2e (118 passed, 2 skipped), packed consumers, and metadata evidence (189 + 481 verified facts) pass. Tests: 2,249 passed, 34 skipped, 1 failed — `packages/ai/test/elements.browser.test.ts` in Firefox after 17.5 s, which passes alone (54) |

**Findings:** (1) Implicit submission cannot reach `odd-button`: the HTML default button is the first submit button in tree order, which a form-associated custom element never is. Enter in the form's only text field submits with no submitter, so the button's `name`, `value`, and overrides are missing; `odd-input` blocks implicit submission entirely. Both are documented, and `button.css` is the native alternative. (2) Disabled `odd-button`s kept their appearance's background and border, because `:host([appearance]) button` outranked `button:disabled`; fixed with `:host button:disabled` (+31 B gzip). (3) For a GET form whose button sets `formmethod="post" formenctype="text/plain"`, Chromium 156 sends a urlencoded body labelled `text/plain`, while Firefox 157 and WebKit 27.2 send the text/plain encoding. Native submit buttons in Chromium do the same, so the spec compares each `odd-button` request with a native twin. (4) `requestSubmit()` accepts only native submit buttons, so an `odd-button` cannot be passed as the submitter. (5) A Firefox validation bubble left open by a blocked submission swallowed the next test's click (no click event reached the document). The tests now handle `invalid` and cancel the bubble. (6) The first full run failed a native-button comparison in Firefox: the pointer, left by an earlier test, rested over a newly rendered `odd-button`, so its hover background was compared. Reproduced in all three engines by parking the pointer there and waiting 300 ms. The tests now move the pointer onto plain text and wait for running transitions before comparing. (7) Transient: on 2026-10-18 the new e2e spec timed out in Firefox in three runs while the other agent's suites were running, and the passing Firefox test took 14.5 s. On 2026-10-19 it took 6.5 s alone and passed 24 of 24 repeats. (8) `npm run compat` also refreshed the side-nav structural row (37 → 36 keys) left stale by commit `2c7bb15`.

| Mutation probes | Temporary source edits, reverted | Killed, 3 of 3: the old `var(--odd-card-padding, <step>)` padding rule (static fallback check; padding test in three engines); `--odd-color-surface-default` declared on the card's `:host` (static declaration check; variable and scope tests in three engines); the button radius read without `--odd-button-radius` (static documented-variables check; variable test in three engines) |
| Existing suites | `npx vitest run --project browser` on the card, multi-product, examples, styling, and styling-contract tests | Pass (147) |
| Full pipeline | `npm run verify` steps one by one (`npm test -- --reporter=verbose`, then `npm run verify:metadata`) | Lint (boundaries, CSS compatibility, format), typecheck, metadata evidence (189 + 481 verified facts), size (`components:card` 678 → 668 B), e2e (122 passed, 4 skipped), packed consumers pass. Tests: 2,383 passed, 34 skipped, 1 failed — `button.browser.test.ts` "does not submit when the click is cancelled…" in Firefox, timed out "waiting for click" at its second `userEvent.click`; the file passes alone (48 of 48, twice) |

**Findings:** (1) The theme's component roles `card.padding` and `card.radius` produce `--odd-card-padding` and `--odd-card-radius`, the same names as the card's documented variables. Because the theme always sets them, the card's `padding="none|sm|lg"` rules, written as `var(--odd-card-padding, <step>)`, never applied on a page with the theme: all four steps rendered 24 px in all three engines. The existing card test did not load the theme, so it passed. The steps now set their value directly and `md` reads the role. (2) In the default theme `padding="lg"` (`space.lg`) and `md` (`card.padding`, through `layout.inset`) are both 24 px, so `lg` looks the same as the default. The theme values are unchanged here; this is a design follow-up. (3) Firefox stalls in full runs also hit unmodified suites: button activation and input typing on 2026-10-18, each waiting in `userEvent.click`, and today an AI elements test that only mounts an element and reads text (17.5 s). All of them pass alone. They happened while three browsers and Node ran together; the cause is not identified.

(2) A class cannot both extend `HTMLElement` and take a second base type redeclaring `addEventListener` (TS2320); `this`-polymorphic overloads on `OddkinElement` plus a type-only `_events` member avoid that and need no per-element runtime code. (3) `HTMLElementEventMap` includes `GlobalEventHandlersEventMap`, which side-nav augments, so filtering "native" events by that map dropped `odd-action`; React 19 adds any lowercase `on<name>` prop on a custom element as a listener, so no filter is needed. (4) The keyboard test failed under full load in Firefox before and WebKit now; it retries twice, and a real mismatch fails every attempt. (5) Core's production `define.js` keeps a bare `import "./element.js"` that esbuild ignores with a warning in size builds; it predates this work (same at HEAD in a separate worktree). (6) Not covered: Vue templates (`vue-tsc`) and Svelte markup (`svelte-check`), neither installed.

| Cart example | `npx vitest run --project browser packages/app/test/command.browser.test.ts` | Pass in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit (2 tests). The §8.1 element: Add is disabled while the cart loads and while an addition is pending; a 503 is retried with the same item after the policy delay and the status shows "Retrying Tea (attempt 2)"; a 409 is not retried and the optimistic item is rolled back; Cancel aborts the request, keeps the item, reads the cart again, and the item the server added anyway stays; removing the element aborts the pending request with a reason naming the element, sets `cancelled`, and returns `scopeStats()` to baseline; reconnecting reads the cart again; no `unhandledrejection` event fired. The first Chromium run failed: the test removed and re-appended the element in one task, so the cancelled addition's continuation ran after reconnection and its `cart.refresh()` superseded the request the test answered. The test now lets the continuation run while disconnected (finding 1) |
| Production build | `npx vitest run --project node packages/app` | Pass (52 tests, including the production build): `app.command.disconnected` and `app.command.options` keep their codes in `dist/prod` with the generic message, and the development explanations are absent from `dist/prod`; the root entry re-exports `./command` |
| Mutants | `.tmp/mutate.mjs` (one mutant at a time; original bytes restored and hash-checked) | 28 of 28 killed: `run()` allowed without an owner; the first attempt started in a microtask; `exclusive` not dropping; `queue` as the default; `latest` keeping every waiting input; cancellation returning to `idle` (killed in Node and in the Chromium cart example); late successes and late failures after cancellation committing; cancellation not aborting the attempt or the retry wait; cancellation, owner disposal, or failure aborting without the real reason; one retry more than allowed; `when` ignored; the delay ignored; the wait showing the failed attempt's number; a throwing policy not reported; an invalid computed delay accepted; the timeout never armed; the queue stopping after a settled run; `reset()` clearing a pending run; connecting elsewhere keeping the run; a disposed command reconnecting; `run` tracked by the calling effect; a settled error counting one attempt; `retry` without `when` accepted; disconnection not cancelling (Chromium cart example). The retry wait's own guard was not probed: cancelling disposes the wait's scope and clears its timer, so removing the guard is equivalent |
| Size | `node scripts/check-size.mjs` | `command` 3,723 B gzip with `Scope`, the reactive graph, and diagnostics (budget 4,096 B); a graph guard keeps rendering modules, `@oddkin/state`, and the resource and application modules out of it |
| Pipeline | `npm run typecheck`; `npx vitest run --project node packages/state packages/app tests/architecture`; `npx vitest run --project browser packages/state packages/app`; `npm run verify:packs`; `npx playwright test e2e/plain-html.spec.ts`; `npm run lint:contracts` | Pass: typecheck including tests and framework typings; 128 Node tests; 71 browser tests and 1 skip (WebKit `moveBefore()`); packed consumers import `@oddkin/app/command`; the plain-HTML consumer loads the app root, which now re-exports `command`, in three engines; contracts up to date (§8.1 is outside the contract markers) |

**Findings:** (1) Runs belong to a connection, so moving an element (removal and insertion in one task) cancels its pending mutation; a continuation that re-reads after `cancelled` then reads on the new connection, which is the safe outcome, but a test or application that answers requests by position must account for it. (2) A cancelled read and a cancelled mutation need different terminal states: a resource returns to its prior state, because a read changed nothing, while a command stays `cancelled`, because its effect on the server is unknown. Separating `dropped` (never started) from `cancelled` (started) is what lets a consumer roll back only when the change certainly did not happen.

**Findings:** (1) WebKit refuses more than 100 `pushState`/`replaceState` calls in 10 seconds per document and throws `SecurityError`, so a router must keep history writes few and survive a refused one: a navigation from the top writes one entry, a scroll pause one replacement, and a refused URL abandons the navigation instead of leaving the view and the URL apart. The router tests run in two documents to stay under the limit. (2) A position written into `history.state` during `pagehide` survives a reload only in WebKit; Chromium and Firefox dropped it (`history.state` was `null` after the reload in both), so positions are stored once scrolling pauses. (3) Firefox and WebKit scroll to a fragment before firing `popstate`, Chromium after it, so the position an entry was left at must come from the last `scroll` event, not from `scrollY` at `popstate`. (4) Under heavy load, Playwright's Firefox was the only engine to time out creating pages and to lose track of pages opened by a Ctrl+click; these are recorded as environment limits, not router failures.

**Findings:** (1) A real back/forward cache restoration can be tested only in Chromium here, and only with the full build and without Playwright's `--disable-back-forward-cache`; Playwright's Firefox and WebKit cannot restore pages from the cache, so those engines stay not verified, and a test that merely navigates back proves nothing there. (2) Chromium's order is `pagehide` (persisted), `freeze`, then `resume`, `pageshow` (persisted). Suspending at `pagehide` gives services a chance to close connections before the page is frozen, and treating `resume` as the end of a stay would resume services while the page is still being restored. (3) A browser runs microtasks between the listeners of a native event, so effects can flush between two applications' listeners; restorations must be counted once per event, which synthetic `dispatchEvent` in tests does not reveal by itself. (4) A mutation run that fails without a test summary is not a kill; rerun it before counting it.

| Mutants | `node .tmp/mutate.mjs .tmp/mutants-scope-reasons.json` | 6 of 6 killed: the late signal aborted without the reason, a child created after disposal without it, children disposed with the parent without it, an effect run scope without the owner's reason, the reason not stored, and a later call replacing the first reason. |

**Findings:** (1) The eager `scope.signal` reads in `@oddkin/app` (`resource.ts`, `command.ts`, `router.ts`) remain correct, but their comments describe the old behaviour; they can be simplified when that code is next changed. (2) On this machine `localhost` resolves to `::1` first, so the Vitest browser server listens on IPv6 only. In a full `npm test` run Firefox could not open one test session (`NS_ERROR_CONNECTION_REFUSED`; the other 2,199 tests passed), one Firefox-only run ended with an error before any test ran, and two three-engine runs stalled without output and were stopped; each engine alone then passed. The IPv6-only listener is the suspected cause, not yet confirmed or fixed. Earlier entries record the same symptom ("Firefox failed to connect to its browser session").

The `products-density` theme adopted in the document; each probe's colour, surface, link, `space.md`, `layout.gap`, `navigation.item.min-height`, and `navigation.item.padding.inline` equal `resolveToken` for the expected context: a product on the shadow host; mode, product, density, and two profiles on light-DOM ancestors through two nested shadow roots; a density attribute inside a shadow tree ignored without the CSS adopted there and applied with it (also a nested light mode); slotted content taking the mode and product around its slot instead of its light-DOM parent's; a nested `data-odd-theme` resetting an outer product while keeping dark mode. A final test asserts that each pair of probes differs in the axis it tests. |
| Tokens Node tests | `npx vitest run --project node packages/tokens` | Pass — 85 tests, including a guard that no token name names a physical direction. |
| Mutants | 6 mutants in `css.ts`, run against the new test alone | 6 of 6 killed: inverted dark toggle, light scope without its mode closure, scopes declaring only changed tokens, exact instead of `~=` profile matching, and (after moving the theme case under a product, because the first version did not kill it) the theme selector dropped from the base block. |

**Finding:** with the generated CSS adopted inside a shadow root (not the documented setup, which adopts it in the document), a profile on a light-DOM ancestor is lost inside a nested scope in that shadow tree: the scope re-declares base expressions and the profile's re-application selector cannot cross the boundary (`layout.gap` 15 px instead of 10 px in Chromium and WebKit). Pinned by the `profile-lost` / `profile-repeated` cases and documented in theming-and-styling.md §5.3 with the workaround (repeat `data-odd-profile` on the inner scope). A fix would need profile toggles like the mode toggles; not attempted.

**Direction:** no token name contains a physical direction; apps/docs, examples/router, and examples/tokens-css-only use no physical margin, padding, border, or offset properties (searched). Component `dir="rtl"` evidence belongs to the component lane.

**Figma-side issues, for the owner (in addition to the previous entry):**

1. Floating surfaces disagree. Popover and toast use `surface.default` with `Elevation/lg`. The menu uses `surface.raised` with no shadow. The tooltip uses `surface.raised` with `control/radius`. 3. The neutral tone's foreground is `text.secondary` in badges and `text.primary` in alerts.

5. The radio and switch focus rings use an unbound literal radius (10003) instead of `radius/full`.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Browser tests | `npx vitest run --project browser packages/core/test/position.browser.test.ts` | 13 tests pass in Chromium 156, Firefox 157, and WebKit 27.2 (39): placed before the next frame; start alignment in both directions and centring; flip to the opposite side, and no flip when turned off; shift inside the viewport margin; inline sides through the direction; block sides through `vertical-rl`; room reported on the side used; scroll containers outside a shadow root followed only while open; anchor resizing followed; nothing after scope disposal; a surface already open when connected; the surface stays in place and inherits a custom property and `dir`. |
| Mutation probes | 15 mutants (`.tmp/mutate.mjs`, Chromium) | 15 of 15 killed: no flip, no shift, direction ignored, writing mode ignored, close not stopping, scroll containers not found, light-DOM parents only, placement after a task, anchor size not observed, disposal still listening, centring ignored, offset ignored, viewport margin ignored, already-open surface not placed, room measured across. Three survived a first run because the size observer's first delivery re-placed the surface; the tests now wait for it before changing layout. |
| Size | `node scripts/check-size.mjs` | New entry `position`: 3,549 B gzip (budget 3,840). Scope with the reactive graph and diagnostics alone is 2,303 B, so the controller adds about 1.25 KiB. Other entries unchanged (counter 9,531, composite 11,876). |
| Contracts, boundaries, types, format | `node scripts/build-contracts.mjs`; `npm run lint:contracts`; `npm run lint:boundaries`; `npx tsc -b packages/core`; `npx prettier --check` | Pass. `./controllers/position` is a DOM-free entry (no DOM access at import). `tsconfig.tests.json` reports errors only in another agent's in-progress file (packages/components/test/figma-reuse.test.ts). |

**Change:** `PositionController` places a `popover` surface against an anchor from measured rectangles: logical `side` and `align` resolved through the anchor's writing mode and direction, `offset`, `flip`, `shift`, `viewportMargin`, coordinates written through the CSSOM, and `onPlace`/`placement` reporting the room on each axis. It starts on `beforetoggle` to open (placing in a microtask, before paint) and stops on `beforetoggle` to close; while open it listens to the window, the visual viewport, and each scroll container of the anchor in the composed tree, and observes both sizes. core-contracts §4.1 and css-architecture.md §9 updated.

**Remaining:** native anchor positioning backend (ADR 0044 §4, an enhancement above the floor); pinch zoom (visual viewport offsets) and transformed ancestors are not exercised; floor browsers at runtime (deferred by the owner). First users: Agent 4's overlay components.

**Findings:** manual slot assignment lets each panel sit inside its own `tabpanel` wrapper in the tabs' shadow root, so `aria-controls`/`aria-labelledby` resolve in one tree (css-architecture.md §12.1, pattern 1) while the panel content stays in the light DOM. Not verified: screen-reader output, real devices, and Safari on macOS.

**Findings:** Figma has three surface treatments. Anchored overlays use the raised surface, `control.radius`, and the `Oddkin/Overlay` effect (`elevation.md`). Modal overlays use the default surface, `card.radius`, and `Elevation/xl`. Toasts use the modal surface with `Elevation/lg`. One module covers the first two: the class `overlay-surface` for inner `[popover]` and `<dialog>` elements, and `:host([popover])` for elements that are themselves popovers (odd-popover, odd-tooltip, odd-toast). In the default light theme the raised and default surfaces are the same colour; only dark mode tells them apart, so the dark-mode test is the one that holds the choice. Enter and exit motion is added with odd-popover, with its gates. Not verified: screen-reader output, real devices, and Safari on macOS.

Popovers fade in with a keyframes animation at the floor instead, and fade out behind the `transition-behavior` gate (registry entries `popover-api` and `starting-style` are now implemented, with tests). `showPopover({ source })`, which tells the browser that the anchor is the invoker, is above the floor (ADR 0044). The wiring gets the same behaviour at the floor by remembering a press on the anchor while the surface is open. Not verified: screen-reader output, real devices, Safari on macOS, and iOS light dismiss (the close button is the floor exception's remedy).

## 2026-10-23 — `PositionController` and native invokers (core-contracts.md §4.1)

**Environment:** Windows, Node 24.22.1, Vitest 5.0.5, Playwright 1.64.1 (Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2). Other agents' uncommitted work in the same tree (Agent 2's `odd-dialog`).

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reproduction | `npx vitest run --project browser packages/core/test/position.browser.test.ts --browser.name=chromium` before the fix | The new test "places a surface its invoker opens" fails: after a user's click on a `popovertarget` button the popover is open but at the browser's default place (top 423 px instead of 120 px). The `beforetoggle` listener's microtask ran before the surface was showing, so the start saw `:popover-open` false. |
| Fix | same, plus `packages/components/test/popover.browser.test.ts`, three engines | Open now also starts on the next animation frame, which runs before that frame is painted; a start queued before the scope is disposed does nothing (new test: dispose in the same turn as `showPopover()`, no placement after two frames). 107 runs pass in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, 4 skipped. |
| Mutation probes | `node .tmp/mutate.mjs .tmp/c-mutants-position.json` (Chromium) | 3 of 3 killed: no frame start, no disposal flag, no flag check. |
| Node, contracts | `npm run contracts`; `npx vitest run --project node` | The contracts are regenerated (one section hash). The core and repository node tests pass; the node project's other failures are in uncommitted work (`odd-dialog` metadata not yet built; the import maps lack `@oddkin/core/i18n` for odd-input's dist). |

**Findings:** A popover opened by the browser itself (a declarative invoker) and one opened by script differ in when `beforetoggle`'s microtasks run, so a controller that waits for "shown" in a microtask must also wait for the next frame. Agent 2's overlay wiring works around it on its own; this makes the controller right for every caller. Not verified: Safari on macOS, touch input.

In forced colours the border and the divider (a 1px solid border then) are `CanvasText` and the close glyph `ButtonText`. | Lifetime | `node research/benchmarks/lifetime/run.mjs --cycles 1000` | The component scenario now also connects and removes an open `odd-dialog` each cycle. Timing is not a measured result here (other lanes were running browsers). The results file is the owner's and stays uncommitted. |
| Size, CSS | `node scripts/check-size.mjs`; `npm run compat` | `components:dialog` is 638 B gzip (budget 704); CSS comments ship in the CSS, so the structural notes moved to the doc comment (they had made it 779 B). The dialog and backdrop fades add 34 B to `components:shared`: 3,018 B measured as HEAD plus this change (budget 3,072); the working tree's total is over budget with other lanes' uncommitted control and field styles. The compatibility check passes with 0 problems; the dialog sheets add 2 stylesheets and 3 keys at the floor (`css.properties.display.contents`, `css.properties.inset-block-start`, `css.types.length.viewport_percentage_units_dynamic`). An earlier `forced-color-adjust: none` for the divider failed the check (Safari 17.4); in forced colours the divider is now a `CanvasText` border. |

**Findings:** the native `<form method="dialog">` lookup finds no `<dialog>` for a form slotted into the element (its tree has none), so the wiring closes the dialog on `submit` at the host. Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit all return focus to the previously focused element when a modal dialog closes, before the `close` event; the wiring then moves it to `returnFocus` when given. Safari does not focus a button on a press, so a dialog opened from a press has no opener there; the wiring then blurs the closed dialog's focused element instead of leaving focus inside it. `close()` settles the open state at once, because the `close` event comes a task later and a `show()`/`close()` pair in one task reopened the dialog through the deferred `open` update. Emulated `closedby="none"` cancels `cancel`; Chrome closes anyway on a second Escape with no user activation in between, which the registry entry records. `:open` is not adopted: a dialog's `open` attribute says the same at the floor. Not verified: screen-reader output, real devices, Safari on macOS, and the emulated paths in a browser that lacks `closedby` (tested by removing the property in these engines).

Compatibility check OK: `customizable-select` is implemented with four keys (`appearance: base-select`, `::picker()`, `::picker-icon`, `::checkmark`), each use inside its gate. |

**Findings:** Firefox 149 and later accept `appearance: base-select` without `::picker()` (BCD), so the gate needs both conditions, and the compatibility check wants `selector(::picker` in it for the pseudo-element; `::picker-icon` and `::checkmark` sit behind their own `selector()` gates. WebKit 27.2 draws a `base-select` select in a shadow root with its author styles but `getComputedStyle()` reports unstyled values for it and its options (black text, zero padding, transparent picker); with `appearance: none` the values are reported, so the parity and field tests read the closed control that way in WebKit and the picker is measured by rendered boxes there. Each option's `selected` property follows `value` in the template, so the selection is set in the render, before the form controller reads validity. Not verified: screen-reader output, touch devices, Safari on macOS, and the WebKit strict-CSP report for this element (no strict-CSP page renders it yet; css-architecture.md §10.2 records how a check that does must allow it).

## 2026-10-23 — `odd-toast` (M10, component-contracts.md §3.5; WCAG 2.2.1, 4.1.3; ADR 0044)

**Environment:** Windows, Node 24.22.1, Vitest 5.0.5, Playwright 1.64.1 (Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2). Other work in the same working tree, not in this commit: the owner's Figma snapshot, icon, and layout work, plans, artifacts, and lifetime results files. Browser runs were made one engine at a time.

**Owner decisions (2026-10-23):** each toast is its own `status` (or `alert`) live region with its title as visible text (ADR 0044's open question); open toasts stack in document order, the last at the corner, so reading and Tab order follow the screen; no toast's time runs while any open toast has the pointer or focus.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Behaviour | `npx vitest run --project browser --browser.name=<engine> packages/components/test/toast.browser.test.ts` | 13 tests; all pass in Chromium, 12 in Firefox and WebKit (the accessibility tree is read in Chromium only, through CDP). The host is a `popover="manual"`; shown, it sits `space.md` from the block-end and inline-end edges (the left in right-to-left text, also when narrower than the viewport), 24rem wide within the viewport, and focus stays where it was. Its role is `status`, `alert` for `danger`, with no `aria-label`; the title is visible text and hidden when `label` is empty. The title and message carry `aria-hidden` when it shows and lose it 100 ms later, at each opening (a toast closed before then starts hidden again); Chromium's tree has the `status` region without them at first and with both after. Timing is measured from the `toggle` that starts each clock: the pointer on one open toast holds every open toast past its 3,000 ms, and after it leaves the toast closes within the time it had left, not a fresh duration; focus in one holds it past its 1,500 ms, and the time it had left goes on after focus leaves. A toast that closes does not start a second clock on another. A hidden page counts no time, a toast opened while the page is hidden waits for it to show, a toast opened while another is held waits too, and a closed toast's clock stays stopped. An action in `end`, or `duration="0"`, keeps it open; `duration` is read at each opening, and a toast closed early does not close its next opening. Closed and opened again in one task (a single `toggle`), it starts over: its text leaves the region and joins it again, it is stacked once, and its first clock stops. Open toasts stack in document order, `space.sm` apart, the last at the corner, whatever order they open in; one inserted before the open ones stacks above them while they stay put; closing one moves the ones above it down; taller content restacks them. The close button (`Dismiss`, `strings`) closes it; `open` and `close()` work, and `toggle` reaches the host for each change. In dark mode: the default surface (not the raised one), `card.radius`, `elevation.lg`, the title in UI type and primary text, the message in Small and secondary text, the glyph in the tone colour at `icon.size.md`, padding `space.sm` / `space.md` (block) and `space.md` / `space.sm` (inline), the title centred on the close button's line, the message and action on the next line, the action left of the close button's column, and a long word wrapping. Removed while open and hovered, it closes, leaves the stack, releases the pause (another toast then closes on time), and ownership returns to baseline. |
| Figma parity | `packages/components/test/figma-parity.overlays.browser.test.ts` | odd-toast on Figma `toast` (Success, Danger): the surface fill, stroke, stroke weight, radius, and elevation; the title's and the message's colour and style. The title layer is found by name, so the test reads both HEAD's snapshot and the owner's next one (title under `Header`). The action ("Undo", "Retry") is the author's button; Figma draws the glyphs dark, and Oddkin draws them in the tone colour, as `odd-alert` does. The tooltip parity cases gain `as const`: the test typecheck (`tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json`) failed on them since 5c38376. |
| Catalog-wide | toast, drawer, dialog, popover, tooltip, overlay-surface, and overlay parity files with `examples`, `contract` (CEM), `styling-contract`, `multi-product`, `accessibility`, `description`, one engine at a time | Chromium 668 passed (38 skipped), Firefox 658 (48 skipped), WebKit 658 (48 skipped); no failures. The axe page now holds two open toasts (a `danger` toast, and a `success` toast with an Undo button), audited in light and dark mode. Explained mistake: `tone="error"` is reported, and the toast is neutral and polite. An earlier pass, made while another lane's lifetime benchmark loaded the machine, timed out in Firefox on two toast timing tests (fixed sleeps after showing) and one popover click; the timing tests now measure from the clock's own `toggle`. |
| Node, types | `npx tsc -b packages/components; node scripts/build-metadata.mjs`; `npx vitest run --project node`; `npx tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` | 1,115 node tests pass. `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json` passes; it failed on the tooltip parity cases before this commit. |
| Mutation probes | `node .tmp/mutate.mjs .tmp/n-mutants-toast.json` (Chromium, the toast and overlay parity tests) | 65 mutants over the clock, the shared pause, the stack, the live region, the template, and both sheets, all killed. The first run killed 58 of 64. Four needed tests, now added: an early close cancelling the region's timer, opening while the page is hidden or while another toast is held, and a toast narrower than the viewport at the inline end. Two were equivalent, so that code went: the popover's auto margins are 0 with an auto inset, and `overflow-wrap: anywhere` already meets a `minmax(0, …)` floor. Fixing the one-toggle reopen added three probes; two older ones then survived until a test counted the scope's live timers while the toast is closed. |
| Lifetime | `node research/benchmarks/lifetime/run.mjs --cycles 1000` | The component scenario now also connects and removes an open `odd-toast` (default duration) each cycle. Ownership returned after every batch in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit, and every element rendered (1,000 of 1,000 cycles in each engine). Chromium retained 323 / 284 B per cycle after forced GC in the component scenario. That second figure varies from run to run for the same build: a Chromium-only probe of the component scenario (`.tmp/n-life-probe.mjs`, `.tmp/n-life-probe2.mjs`: the bench with and without its toast, and with single toast statements removed at bundle time) measured 24 to 418 B per cycle in the second batch, with no variant consistently above the others. WebKit skips the navigation scenario, as before. The results file is the owner's and stays uncommitted. |
| Size, CSS | `node scripts/check-size.mjs`; `node scripts/compat/check-css.mjs` | `components:toast` is 589 B gzip (budget 704): the stack, the shared pause, the clock, and the grid; the surface, motion, and close button are the shared overlay module. The toast sheets add 2 stylesheets and 3 compatibility keys (`inset: auto`, `grid-template-areas`, `column-gap`), all at the floor; 0 problems. |

**Findings:** a close and an open in one task reach the element as one `toggle` with no close, so opening starts over (clock, region text, stack entry) rather than assuming it was closed. A popover's first resize observation can come before its `toggle`, so the element restacks on opening as well as on size changes. Removing an open popover hides it without a `toggle`, so the element clears `open` itself. Under another lane's lifetime run, Firefox frames slowed enough that fixed sleeps after showing ate a 400 ms duration; the timing tests now measure from the `toggle` that starts each clock. Not verified: screen-reader output (whether each screen reader announces the region's late text), real devices, Safari on macOS.

## 2026-10-24 — odd-scroll-region (M10, component-contracts.md §3.7; Figma `Oddkin/Layout/ScrollRegion`)

- **What:** `@oddkin/components/scroll-region` (`/foundation`, `/define/scroll-region`). The scroller is part `base` inside the shadow root, so the shared focus-ring module draws its ring and no attribute is added to the host; the host is a one-track `minmax(0, 1fr)` grid with zero minimums, so `block-size` or `max-block-size` on it bounds the scroller and, as a flex or grid item, it takes the space left. While the content overflows (scroll size above client size on either axis), `base` has `tabindex="0"`, `role="region"`, and `aria-label` from `label` or `strings.label` ("Scrollable content"); when it fits, none of them. It measures once in `mounted()` (so the state is right as soon as `updateComplete` resolves) and then on every resize of the scroller or the content wrapper (`@oddkin/core/controllers/observe` `ResizeController`). Children are `layout.gap` apart (`--odd-scroll-region-gap`). `scrollbar-gutter: stable` is gated by `@supports` (Safari 18.2; `docs/compatibility/features.json` entry now implemented, with its test).

It is hidden from assistive technology through `ElementInternals.ariaHidden` (no host attribute). Alone it has Figma's Step status look (`control.height.sm`, `radius.full`, a `border.width.default` ring; action colours when complete, danger when failed); the recipe sizes it to `icon.size.lg` and colours it through `::part(base)`.

In forced colours the connector is `CanvasText` and the markers keep a ring.

Step links keep the text colour and their underline.

## 2026-10-26 — `light-dark()` for colour tokens measured (ADR 0046 D2): not adopted

The generator gains an experimental option, `CssOptions.modeColors: 'light-dark'`. With it, each colour that differs by mode is written once as `light-dark(LIGHT, DARK)`; mode scopes set `color-scheme` and re-declare only what still depends on the toggles. The default (`'toggles'`) is unchanged.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Option | `npx vitest run --project node packages/tokens/test/mode-colors.test.ts` | 5 tests: the default output is byte-identical; each colour that differs by mode becomes `light-dark()` and every other value is unchanged; mode scopes keep only the toggled values (the 4 shadows), not the colour aliases; product colours carry no toggles; a `light-dark()` colour that reads a toggled token through either value stays in the mode scopes. |
| Mutation probes | `node .tmp/n-mutate.mjs .tmp/n-mutants-d2.json` | 9 of 9 killed (option default, colour-only, value order, reference closure, base, scope, and mode-scope compilation). |
| Bytes | `node research/experiments/light-dark/measure.mjs` | `tokens:default.css` 28,155 → 16,775 B raw, 3,067 → 2,899 B gzip (−168). Mode-scope declarations 40 → 4. The `products-density` case is −202 B gzip and the harbor example −195. |
| Equivalence | same script; Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2; light and dark preference; forced colours emulated | Every colour and shadow token compared on 22 probes for each of 3 themes. The probes cover root, light/dark/system scopes nested both ways, products and densities in modes, a profile, a nested theme, several axes on one element, shadow roots with and without adopted CSS, two levels deep, and slotted content. Identical everywhere without forced colours, except the probe with an author `color-scheme: dark` (36 colours flip; by design of `light-dark()`). In forced colours, Chromium is identical. Firefox differs on the light-DOM probes in dark scopes (8 or 10 probes × 36 colours), because it computes `color-scheme` as `normal` on forced elements, so opted-out descendants get light values. WebKit's emulation forces no colours. |
| Parity | same script | `resolveToken` and DTCG output are identical. `emitInspectJson` still describes the toggles, so adoption would need it moved into the token graph. Theme Studio regenerates through `generate()`, which would follow; it takes 6.4 ms instead of 6.1 ms for the default theme. |

**Findings:** Firefox resolves `light-dark()` from a forced `color-scheme: normal` in forced colours, where Chromium keeps the author's scheme (checked with a bare `light-dark()` in each engine). Scripts reading `getPropertyValue('--odd-color-…')` get `light-dark(#6250e8, #b4a8ff)` instead of `#b4a8ff`.

**Decision:** Not adopted (ADR 0046 D2: smaller, but not equivalent). `light-dark-function` returns to declined with this evidence (features.json, css-architecture.md §4.3, theming-and-styling.md §5.1).

**Gaps:** The floor browsers (Chrome 130, Firefox 132) were not run with this script. Real Windows high-contrast themes were not tried; only Playwright's emulation was.

Environment: Windows, Node 24.22.1, Vitest 5.0.5, Playwright 1.64.1 (Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2), HEAD 6883ddf. Other lanes in progress in the tree: Agent 2's composition schema follow-ups and Agent 3's layout recipes.

It is a text input with `role="spinbutton"`, the decimal input mode, `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin`, and `aria-valuemax` (and `aria-valuetext` when the text is not the plain number), and the `stepper` segment of `decrement` and `increment` buttons. The buttons are not Tab stops; a press keeps focus in the field; each is disabled where its step cannot move the value. Up and Down step by `step`, Page Up and Page Down by ten steps, and Home and End go to the ends of the grid when bounded; each move dispatches `input` and `change`. Stepping is HTML's `stepUp()` algorithm in the new shared `src/form-control/range.ts`. `value` is sanitized as a native number field's. Typed text that is not a number stays in the field and fails `badInput` with `strings.badInput` through core `FormValueOptions.badInput`. Range, step, and required validity and their messages come from a detached native number input. Adds `valueAsNumber`, `stepUp(n)`, and `stepDown(n)`. `OddkinTextControl` gains a `_sanitize` hook (the identity for text) and binds the typed text, not the value, to the native field.

## 2026-10-26 — odd-color-picker (M10 round 7, Agent 1, component-contracts.md §3.3)

Environment: Windows, Node 24.22.1, Vitest 5.0.5, Playwright 1.64.1 (Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2), HEAD 120651d. No other lane's work was in the tree.

**Change:** `odd-color-picker` draws Figma `colorPicker` (six variants) and `color/Swatch` (four). HTML's colour input is the baseline: the value is sanitized as a native colour input sanitizes it (any CSS colour, black for none, lowercase `#rrggbb`), and with HTML's `alpha` it is `color(srgb r g b / a)`. The text input shows uppercase hex after the colour's swatch; typed text that is not hex stays, the colour stays, and validity is `badInput` ("Enter a six-digit hex color, such as #2563EB."). The button opens a non-modal dialog joined under the field (the overlay wiring and the overlay-surface module). The dialog holds the saturation-and-brightness area (one `role="slider"`: `aria-valuenow` is the saturation, `aria-valuetext` names both), the hue (a slider in degrees on the shared range pieces), hex entry, opacity entry (a spinbutton, with `alpha` only), the RGB values, suggested colours (native radios from `<option>` children or `options`, through the collection source), and Cancel and Apply (the native-button sheet). Apply commits with one `input` and `change`; Cancel, Escape, or a press outside discard. In forced colours, the swatches, the area, and the hue track keep the user's colours: `forced-color-adjust: none` is a new registered enhancement in `features.json`, gated by `@supports`.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native colour input probe | temporary test, three engines | Chromium and Firefox sanitize to lowercase `#rrggbb`, parse any CSS colour, and give `#000000` for text that is no colour and by default. No engine implements `alpha`; Firefox takes `colorspace="display-p3"`; Playwright's WebKit on Windows has no colour type. `required` gives no `valueMissing` |
| odd-color-picker | `npx vitest run --project browser color-picker.browser.test.ts`, three engines | Chromium 26 of 26; Firefox 25 passed, 1 skipped (forced colours runs in Chromium only); WebKit 24 passed, 2 skipped (also the comparison with a native colour input). The value matches a native colour input for twelve inputs in Chromium and Firefox |
| Figma parity | `figma-parity.pickers.browser.test.ts`, three engines | colorPicker Closed, Custom hex, Disabled, Focus, Invalid, Open; color/Swatch Default, Disabled, Focus, Selected: no differences. One deliberate: the swatch's fill is the user's colour, which Figma binds to no role |
| Catalog-wide, three engines | color-picker, pickers parity, accessibility, contract, description, examples, keyboard, multi-product, styling-contract, styling | First run: two failures in each engine, both mine: the `alpha` example's value did not survive a round trip (now written as `color(srgb …)`), and the contract test counted `alpha` as a constraint that makes the element invalid (now excluded, with the reason). Rerun of `examples` and `contract`: 806 passed, 50 skipped in each engine; the other files passed in the first run |
| Mutation probes | `node .tmp/mutate.mjs .tmp/f-mut-cp.json` (Chromium; three focus probes on WebKit) | 76 probes over the class, the colour functions, the template, and both sheets, after adding tests for modified keys, keys the area ignores, the hue through a grey, the primary button only, the hue's inset, the check's contrast, invalid suggestions, and opacity bounds. 75 killed; the survivor (opacity text with its percent sign in one input event) got a test and is killed. One dead branch removed: Apply's check for invalid hex (the button is disabled then) |
| Node, types, metadata | `npx tsc -b packages/components`; `node scripts/build-metadata.mjs`; `node scripts/build-composition-schemas.mjs --check`; `node scripts/check-vocabulary.mjs`; `npx vitest run --project node`; `npm run typecheck` | First metadata build: four guidance warnings (colour syntax in backticks read as method and attribute references), reworded. Node first run: 1 failure, mine (the reuse map's class counts), fixed; final run 1,235 of 1,235. Composition 53 elements, 54 schemas. Vocabulary 0 findings. Typecheck passes |
| Size, CSS | `node scripts/check-size.mjs`; `npm run compat` | `components:color-picker` 1,644 B gzip, budget 1,664. Compat 0 problems after the enhancement was registered (190 stylesheets, 325 keys) |
| Lifetime | `node research/benchmarks/lifetime/run.mjs --scenario componentCycles` | Ownership returned in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit; 1,000 rendered in each. Chromium retained 371 / 166 B/cycle |

**Findings:**
- The value format follows HTML's text for `alpha`, which no engine implements yet; `colorspace="display-p3"` (Firefox only) is not offered: a recorded limitation.
- The compatibility policy had no opt-out from forced colours ("no forced-color-adjust opt-out is used", the `system-colors` entry). A colour picker shows nothing useful when its colours become system colours, so the opt-out is registered as an enhancement used only for user colour data. The `system-colors` entry's sentence is not mine to change; it is noted for the owner.
- WebKit does not focus a button or a radio on a click: Apply, Cancel, and the suggested colours focus themselves, so focus returns to the field's button when the popup closes.
- Figma always draws the opacity field; the element shows it only with `alpha`, as HTML gives a colour input an alpha component. Figma labels the swatches "Recent colors"; the element's default is "Suggested colors" (`strings.swatches`), since the page supplies them.
- Not verified: screen-reader output (the area's value text), real touch drags, Safari on macOS.

## 2026-10-26 — Real-browser text entry (Agent 1, M8)

Environment: Windows, Node 24.22.1, Vitest 5.0.5, Playwright 1.64.1 (Chromium 156, Firefox 157, WebKit 27.2).

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Text entry and the elements' own tests | `packages/components/test/{text-entry,input,textarea,one-time-code,color-picker,figma-parity.forms,figma-parity.pickers}.browser.test.ts`, three engines | Chromium 238/238; Firefox 231 + 7 skipped (Chromium-only IME); WebKit 230 + 8 skipped |
| Mutation probes | 21 probes on the changed source, Chromium, `text-entry.browser.test.ts` | 20 killed; 1 survivor (below) |
| Size | `node scripts/check-size.mjs` | input 511/576, one-time-code 614/640, textarea 264/320, color-picker 1,698/1,728 |

**Observed:**
- Typing the same keys into odd-input (text, email, url, tel, search, password, number) and odd-textarea gives the same `input` events, `inputType`s, values, and `change` as the native field, in all three engines.
- The caret and selection survive a re-render (error, placeholder, label) and the same value set again, as native. A new value set from script while the field has focus keeps the caret where it was (`live()`); a native field moves it to the end. Deliberate.
- Full-width digits (`１２．５`) read as the native number field reads them in all three engines; the one-time code and the colour picker's hex and opacity read them too.
- IME (Chromium, `Input.imeSetComposition` then `Input.insertText`): composed text is not committed before it ends; the number field, the one-time code (cells show only digits while composing), and the colour picker's field and hex end with the final text; arrow and Escape keys pressed while composing are left to the input method. **Firefox and WebKit: not tested; no driver.**
- Autofill: `autocomplete` reaches the native field (input, textarea, one-time code default `one-time-code`, colour picker `off`); a value set as autofill sets it (value, then `input` and `change`) reaches the value, validity, events, and `FormData`. `:autofill` and `:-webkit-autofill` are supported in all three engines; no element styles them, so each engine's own autofill look shows.

**Fixed:** the one-time code lost IME text, dropped full-width digits, and left the caret mid-code after a script set; the number field ignored full-width digits, stepped or cleared on keys pressed while composing, and fired `change` when only its text changed; the colour picker ignored full-width hex and opacity; odd-textarea kept CR from script.

**Survivor:** the one-time code's `input.value === this.value` guard in `updated()` (no caret move while composing). A CDP composition is not disturbed by a selection change, so no test can show it; kept for real input methods.

**Findings:** (1) Firefox 157's `moveBefore()` keeps a focused element's focus in the light DOM but blurs it inside a shadow root (a probe: no exception, `activeElement` null afterwards), so `repeat()` lost focus in a shadow-root list; it now restores focus after any move that lost it. (2) WebKit's fallback restored the selection without its direction (a backward selection became forward); the direction is kept now. (3) A `repeat()` item template that threw left the rows created before it in the DOM, untracked, so the next good list showed an extra row; keys and templates are now evaluated before the DOM changes. (4) A template that failed while committing (a binding rejecting its value) kept its earlier bindings subscribed with no owner; they are released now, and the part stays empty until the next good value. Keeping the previous content instead would need the new template built before the old one is released, which reverses the order refs see (a shared `createRef()` would end `undefined`): not done.

Two were redundant timer cancels (the close timer re-checks hover and focus when it fires), removed from the code. The other five became tests: the 250 ms close delay, focus in the card keeping it open, staying closed after Escape, `interest` off, focus not pulled from outside, and controls wrapping without overlap. All six rerun: killed |

**Findings:**
- Browsers return focus to where it was when a popover opened. A hover card the pointer opened therefore sent focus away from its anchor on Escape, so the card now moves focus to its anchor itself.
- WebKit, as Safari, does not keep focus on a clicked button. The carousel keeps keyboard focus on next once it is unavailable at the last slide, so that test now uses the keyboard.
- Playwright cannot see ElementInternals roles; the carousel's region, label, and role description are read through a probe subclass, as on odd-card.

| Experiment | `node research/experiments/dsd-first-paint/run.mjs --samples 9` (Chromium 156; workspace served through Playwright routes) | Results in `research/benchmarks/results/dsd-first-paint-2026-10-28.json` and the experiment README. Upgrade-only versus prerendered with stylesheet links (strict CSP) versus prerendered with inline styles: CLS 0.040 → 0 (components-only) and 0.138 → 0 (content page); LCP 124 → 120 / 148 ms and 124 → 324 / 168 ms with modules at once, 132 → 144 / 184 ms and 132 → 236 / 228 ms with each module delayed 800 ms; style recalculation +2–8 ms; HTML +3.2–4.2 KB (links) or +26–28 KB (inline). Every shadow root after the upgrade equals the upgrade-only page's, template markers aside |

**Findings:** (1) The first comparison reported every page as different after the upgrade: template part markers (`<!--oddkin-…-->`) carry a per-load nonce, so the check now ignores comments. (2) The upgrade-only content page's layout shift (0.138) is above the 0.1 counted as good: undefined elements render their light DOM inline until they upgrade. Reserving their boxes in page CSS is the cheaper fix; prerendering is not adopted (no LCP gain). Measured on a machine shared with other agents' test runs; the medians of alternating loads are compared, not absolute times.

That is about 921 B raw and 123 B gzip per product, one rule each, of 23 declarations (20 for one brand) |

**Findings:**
- odd-side-nav keys its recipe-local query to its own container (40rem), not to the theme's `navigation.expanded` (the `shell` container, 48rem). A theme that moves `navigation.expanded` leaves the side-nav's breakpoint where it is. layout-recipes.md describes `when` keys as named conditions, so this is a recipe-local exception, recorded in the plan.
- On the shipped default theme, a product rule re-declares the brand and neutral ramps and `color.selection.surface` only. `default.theme.json` pins the approved roles (actions, links, the focus ring, surfaces, text, tones) as overrides, so a product that sets only `brand.primary` keeps the base's primary actions and links. `products.test.ts` builds its base from `brand.primary` alone, without overrides, so it does not show this. Recolouring a product's roles needs product role overrides, the known M9 gap (multi-product.md §9). The growth numbers there are updated. The M4 numbers (41 declarations per product) were measured before the default theme pinned the approved palette (ADR 0041).
- Remaining for the multi-product review: the role compatibility check (ADR 0043 point 5) and candidate v1 contracts for the customization levels.
