## 2026-11-04 — CI on 26504cd: `odd-table`'s `direction` and the stale kits (round 11, Agent 3)

Agent 1's report (lanes, 13:43): on CI run 41911756609, `npm run verify:metadata`, the golden path in three engines, and `npm run verify:packs` failed, and the kits in the packed packages differed from the kits regenerated from them (25 of 68 files in `@oddkin/ai`, 56 of 108 in `@oddkin/components`).

Cause: `odd-table`'s `direction` property, a name ADR 0045's vocabulary keeps for orientation. `verify:metadata` runs `verify-metadata.mjs`, which attaches the browser evidence to each package's metadata, then `check-vocabulary.mjs`, then `package-kits.mjs`. The vocabulary check failed, so the kits were not rewritten after the evidence was attached, and every later comparison of the kits with the metadata failed. The property is now `sortDirection` (attribute `sort-direction`), and `odd-sort`'s detail is `{ column, sortDirection }`. No published version had the old name: 1.0.0-beta.1 predates `odd-table`.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vocabulary | `node scripts/check-vocabulary.mjs` | Before: `vocabulary.synonym <odd-table> direction: use orientation instead of "direction"`, 1 finding. After: 0 findings |
| Evidence, three engines | `browser-set.mjs` on both contract tests, the table test, and the accessibility test | 1,008 passed and 54 skipped in each of Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit; the evidence records are current |
| CI's metadata step | `npm run verify:metadata` | Exit 0: 2,219 verified facts across 55 elements and 481 across 24, no vocabulary findings, and the kits written (68 and 108 files) |
| Packed consumers | `npm run verify:packs` | OK with the evidence attached: the agent kits match their packed metadata in `@oddkin/ai` and `@oddkin/components` (149.9 and 374.3 KiB unpacked) |
| Golden path, three engines | `e2e/golden-path.spec.ts` through the e2e lock | 21 passed |
| Gates | `npm run typecheck`; `npm run lint`; node tests for the components, Workbench's Theme Studio, `tests/agent-run`, and `tests/docs` | Exit 0 (with the previous commit); exit 0; 516 passed and 1 skipped (25 files) |

## 2026-11-04 — Item 7: the Components page reached from the home keeps its sidebar (round 11, Agent 3)

The owner's report (relayed by Agent 1, lanes 13:20): on www.oddkin.dev, the home, then Components in the header, shows the catalog with no sidebar and against the left edge; the home, then Foundations, and Foundations, then Components, show the sidebar.

## 2026-11-04 — `resolveTokens(theme, context)` (round 11, Agent 3)

For Theme Studio's Worker (Agent 2, lanes, 2026-11-03 18:08): every literal for one context in one pass, importable by URL in a Worker. `resolveTokens` returns a `Map` from each token name, in the theme's order, to what `resolveToken(theme, name, context)` gives; a token that does not resolve (a missing reference or a cycle) is left out, as `resolveToken` gives it no value. **Per-change BUDGET review:** existing policy permits measured foundation-reuse increases per change. The independent review found that the new response graph reuses public Popover, the existing Overlay/PositionController and FocusRecovery rather than duplicating their behavior in Citation. Reconstructed baseline at `de271436`: response 24,570 B gzip and chat 64,481. Citation adds 4,283 B to response and 4,467 to chat; the Question fieldset correction adds another 6 B to chat, final 68,954 (+4,473 total). The caps are the smallest 64-byte steps above the measurements: response 28,864 and chat 68,992. Private overlay duplication and asynchronous first-open registration were considered and rejected as more complex. This records an engineering implementation and independent budget review for integration, not a claim that release approval or publishing occurred. OTP's redundant grid was simplified legitimately: its CSS is 630 B versus baseline 614, within the unchanged 640 B cap.

**Findings corrected:** ComboBox's internal box and OTP's native-input intrinsic minimum prevented useful shrinking; Question's native fieldset minimum caused local overflow; resize feedback sizing wrote during observer delivery; citation close/presentation/source updates could drop logical focus; lab selection/reset races could operate on stale examples; parent viewport changes could scroll active iframe work out of view. Regression tests exercise actual controls. A suspected missing Citation fixture dependency was disproved by a fresh source-reveal flow and the hardened unknown-tag sweep; no defect or unnecessary define-all workaround was recorded.

**Limits:** rendering defaults is not exhaustive interaction conformance. Backend outcomes are simulated in authored fixtures; no real service, full localization/text-size matrix, manual screen-reader or touch-device study, cross-document adoption guarantee, or new Figma popover parity is claimed. Parent Flow/Bounded labels remain private docs composition choices, not a public adaptive engine or invented component props. Other existing repository suites were not all rerun.
